name: Jeremiah Van Rensselaer
bio: A Representative from New York; born in New York on August 27, 1738; completed preparatory studies at the manor house, ``Rensselaerswyck,'' and in private schools in Albany; graduated from Princeton College, Princeton, N.J., in 1758; served in the Revolutionary War, ensign and paymaster; member of the Albany, N.Y., Committee of Safety; elected to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Second Congress in 1790; member of the New York state assembly in 1789; member of the first board of directors of the Bank of Albany in 1792 and president of that bank 1798-1806; lieutenant governor of New York 1801-1804; curator of the Evangelical Lutheran Seminary at Albany in 1804; died on February 19, 1810, in Albany, N.Y.; interment in the Dutch Reformed Cemetery; reinterment in Albany Rural Cemetery, Menands, N.Y.
